name: Museum der Wahrnehmung
kurzbeschreibung: The interactive sensory exhibition in Sölden fascinates visitors with hands-on perception experiments, optical illusions, and alpine high-altitude science.
beschreibung:
Overview

The interactive Sensory and Perception Exhibition in Sölden in the rear Ötztal valley offers visitors of all ages an intriguing interplay between sensory physiology, physical natural laws, and alpine perception. Perched at over 1,350 meters above sea level in the vibrant center of the tourism hub of Sölden, this modern interactive space invites visitors to put their own senses to the test. Sight, hearing, touch, balance, and spatial orientation are playfully challenged across diverse experimental stations. This weather-independent world fuses exact natural sciences with astonishing sensory illusions, greatly enhancing the valley's cultural offerings for families, school children, and mountain enthusiasts.

Route & Requirements

The engaging tour leads through themed experiential rooms hosting over fifty interactive exhibits designed for active participation. Guests explore mysterious mirror chambers with seemingly infinite reflections, test 3D optical illusions, and experience acoustic phenomena at parabolic whispering disks and acoustic sound dishes. Tactile pillars and dynamic balance beams demonstrate how the human brain filters and processes sensory information. A special educational focus highlights human and animal perception in the high alpine peaks: How do colors, sound waves, and scents behave in thin mountain air above three thousand meters? What remarkable sensory adaptations allow ibexes, chamois, and ptarmigans to survive on extreme cliffs? Visitors discover captivating answers.

Visit & Arrival

The sensory exhibition is open daily from 10:00 to 18:00 during the official summer and winter seasons (last entry at 17:00). Admission fees: adults approx. €12.00, children and youth €7.50, family passes from €26.00; free or discounted access with the Ötztal Inside Summer Card. Arrival by car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Ötztal) and federal road B186 approximately 35 kilometers into the valley to Sölden; parking is available in the underground garages at Zentrum or Gaislachkogl. By rail and bus: ÖBB train to Ötztal station, then VVT bus route 4194 departing every half hour directly to the Freizeit Arena stop.

Tips

All exhibition spaces are step-free and fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers, featuring multilingual explanation boards in German and English. Allocate at least an hour and a half to try out the hands-on sensory stations. An exceptional rainy-day activity that pairs seamlessly with swimming at the Freizeit Arena Sölden adventure pool or taking a scenic cable car ride up to Gaislachkogl peak.
